title: Midnight Bridge outreach sketch
body:
Quick personal scratchpad for Midnight Bridge (MB) outreach — keep raw, update after calls.

Context / thesis:
- MB = "Midnight Bridge Labs" (analytics platform + marketplace for retail risk models). They recently raised a Series B (press from Oct 2025) and have public docs about an API-first plugin architecture.
- Why they might care: MB needs low-latency, cost-predictable inference for in-product model recommendations + summary generation for analyst workflows. They value throughput for batched scoring and want predictable billing for enterprise customers.

Primary contacts (found via LinkedIn + job page):
- Claire Han — Head of Product Integrations (likely champion)
- Omar Delgado — Engineering Manager, Inference Platform (technical lead)
- Maya Lee — Head of Partnerships (procurement + GTM)

Quick notes from reconnaissance:
- Tech stack hints: AWS + EKS, mention of TF + PyTorch models in their docs, custom model repo + feature store.
- Problem signals: posts about work on "reduce cost of feature scoring" and "improve SLAs for real-time recommendations".
- Procurement red flag: they have existing discounts with a cloud vendor; cost sensitivity for per-token pricing likely high.

Value angles to test in outreach (prioritized):
1) Dedicated capacity pitch (predictable throughput + reserved GPU pools) — emphasize SLA and billing predictability.
2) Smart routing + fallback for multi-region reliability — call out outages during holiday spikes (retail use case).
3) Prefix/KV caching benefits for repeated user contexts — easy wins on per-request cost.
4) Quick proof-of-value: 2-week pilot on a small reserved pool, measurable P50/P95 latency improvements and per-op cost delta.

Outbound draft (cold email skeleton — short):
Subject ideas:
- "Reduce model serving cost for Midnight Bridge's recommendation flows"
- "A quick pilot to stabilize MB inference latency"

Email: 
Hi Claire —
I read about Midnight Bridge's API-first model marketplace and wanted to share a quick idea: Redwood can run a short pilot on a small dedicated pool and show (1) single-digit P95 latency for your recommendation callers, and (2) a predictable per-day bill for reserved capacity.
Would you be open to a 20–30 min sync next week to see if this is a fit?
Best,
Sofia

Cadence idea (3–4 touches):
- Day 0: Short cold email to Claire (above).
- Day 3: Follow-up — add a one-pager summary (attach).
- Day 7: Quick LinkedIn note + ask for intro to Omar (technical).
- Day 14: Last touch — share a short case study (similar retailer).

Meeting prep checklist (if we get time with Omar):
- Ask: current QPS, P95 latency, typical sequence lengths, and cache patterns.
- Infra: on-prem vs cloud, GPU types, autoscaling pains.
- Data security: Does MB want VPC/private control plane or is hosted ok?
- Success metric: 20% token-cost reduction or P95 < 200ms for 90% of requests.
- Demo plan: show dedicated pool + prefix cache on a small sample model; compare to their baseline using synthetic traces.

Possible objections + rebuttals (short):
- "We already use cloud vendor endpoints" -> acknowledge, then point to reserved capacity argument: predictable costs, SLA, and integration for prefix caching that vendor endpoints lack out-of-the-box. Offer side-by-side run for one week.
- "Security / compliance concerns" -> highlight Private deployment (VPC/HSM options) and offer NDA + SOC docs.
- "Too expensive / hard to migrate" -> propose pilot that uses a single model and small reserved pool; show unit economics with our Optimize recommendations.

Pilot scoping (one-pager items to send if they ask):
- Goals: measure P50/P95, per-op cost, and error rates across traffic shapes.
- Duration: 2 weeks (1 week baseline capture, 1 week Redwood run).
- Requirements from MB: sample model artifact (or compatible model name), representative traffic trace (or a lighter synthetic load), and access to a sandbox environment or staging endpoint.
- Redwood deliverables: infra setup, dashboard access, rollbacks, and a short post-mortem with recommended batching/quantization levers.

Signals that make this a high-priority pursuit (internal):
- They run retail analytics (higher QPS during events).
- They have a marketplace — possibility for multi-account upsell (platform + partners).
- Public hiring for "inference optimization" role (investment in scale).

Open questions (to resolve in discovery):
- What are their current contracts / committed spend with cloud vendors?
- Do they host customer models on behalf of customers (multi-tenant inference)? If yes, security becomes critical and private deployment convo accelerates.
- Which models (open vs proprietary) power their recommendation flows?

Next steps (my todo):
- Draft one-pager tailored to MB (deadline: 2026-03-04).
- Pull a 1-paragraph case study about a retail client with similar QPS (ask Priya).
- Prep a short runbook for a 2-week pilot signoff (include compliance checklist).
- Put a Remind in calendar: follow up if no response by 2026-03-10.

Random scratch ideas (kept for brainstorming):
- Offer a "predictable-holiday-pack" — temporary burst capacity priced as a committed short window for their partners.
- Co-marketing angle with Maya (partnerships): "Redwood + Midnight Bridge: stable inference for model marketplaces" — could drive GTM if pilot shows value.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc conversational; move polished materials into shared_drives/company/mkt when ready.
_post_write_notes: Created as a users/ scratchpad — rough language on purpose. Update after calls and remove PII if shared.
